title: Your Computer Is Basically a Very Fast Idiot
subtitle: It renders movies, runs games, and holds video calls — by doing one mind-numbingly simple thing a few billion times a second.
hook: Here's a secret that'll change how you see every device you own: your computer is *stupid*. Gloriously, relentlessly stupid. It does not "run apps" or "understand" anything. It does exactly one tiny thing — grab an instruction, do it, grab the next — and it does it so blindingly fast that the result *looks* like intelligence. Once you see the trick, computers stop being magic and start being obvious. Welcome to lesson one.

sections.heading: The dumbest loop in the world
sections.body:
At the heart of your machine is the **CPU**, and all it ever does is spin one loop:

1. **Fetch** the next instruction.
2. **Decode** it (add? compare? jump?).
3. **Execute** it — usually nudging one or two numbers.

Then back to step 1. Forever. A few *billion* times a second. Every game, browser, and AI you've used is just a monstrously long to-do list of these baby steps. The CPU never knows it's "playing a video." It only ever sees: *next.*

sections.caption: The entire machine, honestly. A pointer tracks where you are; each turn fetches one instruction, does it, and moves on.
sections.mermaid:
flowchart LR
    PC["Where am I?\n(program counter)"] --> F["FETCH\ngrab instruction"]
    F --> D["DECODE\nwhat is it?"]
    D --> E["EXECUTE\ndo the tiny thing"]
    E --> U["move to next"]
    U --> PC
    style F fill:#cfe3ff,stroke:#2b6cb0,color:#111
    style E fill:#cfe3ff,stroke:#2b6cb0,color:#111

sections.label: The whole trick
sections.body: Speed + simplicity, faked hard enough, *becomes* intelligence. The CPU isn't clever — it's just tireless and absurdly fast. Every "smart" thing computers do is millions of dumb steps stacked into a tower. Remember that and nothing in tech will ever intimidate you again.

sections.heading: Why nobody writes billions of instructions by hand
sections.body: They don't — they build **layers**, each one a *convenient lie* that hides the mess below: raw machine code → languages like Python → the operating system → the app you tapped. When you type `print("hi")`, you're standing on a skyscraper of these lies, and at the very bottom floor is that same dumb fetch-decode-execute loop, sweating away. The whole art of software is picking which floor to stand on.

sections.caption: Four minutes watching the fetch-execute loop do its thing. It really is that simple down there.

takeaways: A CPU only ever does one loop: **fetch → decode → execute**, then repeat.
Every program is a giant list of these tiny steps; the CPU sees no 'big picture'.
'Intelligence' is just simple steps run **stupidly fast** — not cleverness.
Software hides complexity in **layers**, each lying about the one below.
`print("hi")` sits atop a tower that bottoms out in that same dumb loop.

quiz.q: What does a CPU actually do, all day, forever?
options: Understands your goals and plans ahead
Runs one app at a time from start to finish
quiz.explain: That's the whole engine — one tiny loop, a few billion times a second.

quiz.q: Why call an abstraction layer a 'convenient lie'?
options: It slows the computer down on purpose
It hides the messy layer below so you can think bigger
quiz.explain: Each layer lets you ignore what's beneath it — right down to raw instructions.

quiz.q: BOSS: A friend says 'AI is smart because the chip understands language.' What's the honest correction?
options: The chip still just does dumb tiny steps, incredibly fast; 'understanding' is the tower built on top
It understands English but not other languages
quiz.explain: No single step is smart. The apparent intelligence is millions of simple operations stacked up — the exact theme of this lesson.

tg_quiz.correct: Yep — one dumb loop, billions of times a second.
tg_quiz.wrong: Nope — it just loops: fetch, decode, execute.
tg_quiz.explain: Everything 'smart' is that tiny loop stacked into a tower.
